title: 1981 Greater London Council election
summary: Labour regained control of the Greater London Council, winning 50 of the 92 seats. The morning after the result the moderate Labour leader Andrew McIntosh was deposed by the left-winger Ken Livingstone, who became leader of the GLC. It proved to be the final GLC election: Margaret Thatcher's government abolished the council in 1986.
highlights: Labour wins control with 50 of 92 seats
Ken Livingstone replaces Andrew McIntosh as leader the day after the poll
The Liberals win a single seat on 14.4% of the vote
The last election ever held to the Greater London Council

council.note: 92 single-member electoral divisions, each coterminous with a Greater London parliamentary constituency. The GLC was abolished by the Local Government Act 1985, taking effect in 1986.
